lines.text: Your outlet gives you about 120 volts. The long distance lines behind it run above a hundred thousand. Why so extreme?
Wires waste energy as heat, and the waste depends on the current flowing through them.
Double the current, and the heat loss doesn't double. It quadruples.
Power is voltage times current. So if you crank the voltage way up, you can send the same power with a tiny current.
Transformers at the power plant boost the voltage, and transformers near your home step it back down.
Those lines are bare metal. The insulation is mostly air, which is why towers are tall and wires are spaced so far apart.
Even so, about five percent of America's electricity is lost along the way.
